findings.reason: The protected implementation is the direct, conventional interview solution: one forward traversal stores the opaque node interfaces, and one stack-pop phase invokes printValue in reverse order. The names nodes and current make the data flow immediate, every control-flow branch is necessary, and no abstraction or trick obscures the immutable-interface constraint. A candidate would not materially improve it.

The first loop appends every node exactly once in head-to-tail order because getNext is the only traversal operation and terminates after the tail. Each later pop removes the last remaining interface, so printValue is called in tail-to-head order. Every node is printed exactly once, the function returns None, and no node value or link is read or mutated directly.

An independent Python oracle reversed only the serialized initialization values, while an opaque audit-node model rejected all access except getNext and printValue and tracked node identities, method counts, and link/value immutability. The oracle, protected solve.py, immutable native leetcode.py, an independently structured cons-stack control, and a repeated-scan control agreed on all eight visible cases, all three benchmark tiers, and all 3,279 nonempty lists of lengths 1 through 7 over {-1, 0, 1}.

Another 10,000 deterministic legal lists generated with seed 1265 matched all four implementations. They included 508 singleton lists, 8,213 with duplicate values, 6,695 containing zero, 9,362 containing a negative value, 9,340 containing a positive value, and 5,029 containing both -1000 and 1000. A separate 1,000-node maximum-length fixture verified the source boundary and exact output multiplicity.

The unchanged hidden tiers define size as immutable-node count at n = 16, 64, and 256, a 16x span. Across three repeated paired runs, the protected implementation passed with extra-growth exponents from +0.00 to +0.01, and an independent O(n) cons-stack control passed from +0.02 to +0.03. A correct O(n log n) divide-and-rescan control passed every ordinary and benchmark output but failed only scaling in all runs at +0.23 to +0.24. The principal O(n^2) constant-space repeated-scan control also produced every benchmark output and failed scaling in all runs at +1.08 to +1.09, with largest-tier ratios from 57.06x to 57.33x. No benchmark edit was warranted.

The three authenticated source examples remain exact visible samples. Two formerly hidden correctness rows are now visible trials, the endpoint-value fixture explicitly covers both -1000 and 1000, and a new 1,000-node trial covers the maximum list length. All eight ordinary rows are visible samples or trials with independently recomputed expected sequences.

The specialized immutable-list validator previously received the function's None return instead of the prepared head whose nodes record printValue calls, causing every correct void implementation to be reported wrong. The result adapter now selects that head for immutable_list_print validation, and focused unit and API regressions cover printed-head selection plus source and maximum-length cases.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode algorithm problem 1265, Python as the primary language, and Solution.printLinkedListInReverse as the verified native entrypoint. Fresh authenticated evidence confirms a nonempty immutable list of 1 through 1,000 nodes, values from -1000 through 1000, exclusive access through getNext and printValue, reverse-order printing, and the no-mutation rule.

The protected app-local and immutable native sources remain unchanged and implement the same node-reference stack, forward getNext traversal, and reverse printValue phase. The native wrapper and type annotation are the only structural adapters. Native source leetcode.py remains bound to verified submission 2068046006, and submission.json was not modified.

The complete Approach was reviewed against both protected sources. It derives storing interfaces rather than unavailable values, explains last-in-first-out reversal and exact-once printing, proves O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space, and covers recursion, constant-space O(n^2) scans, block checkpoints, singleton and duplicate values, and forbidden field access. It now also answers both source follow-ups by making the forward-only time-space tradeoff explicit.

The modular Reference preserves the opaque ImmutableListNode model, both available methods, serialized-input purpose, no-direct-access and no-mutation restrictions, side-effect-only output contract, all three exact examples, both inclusive constraints, and both follow-up questions in their source order.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed three examples without explanations, two constraints, the two-method interface, two follow-up questions, and no images, tables, diagrams, hints, or notes. source_fidelity.json binds all five modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 36720f952ea0b7fab51bdced0bdd2ab7148869a8646acaa53464f331b7777310 and validates without errors.

coverage: The first three visible samples preserve all authenticated source inputs and outputs exactly and in source order; none of the source examples has an explanation.
Eight visible ordinary fixtures cover one node, two nodes, both value endpoints, duplicates, identical values, mixed signs and zero, and the maximum legal length of 1,000 nodes.

The independent serialized-value oracle and opaque audit-node model verified exact values, reverse node-identity order, one print per node, permitted API access, and unchanged links and values across 3,279 exhaustive small lists and 10,000 seeded random legal lists.

The three unchanged hidden performance-only tiers use n = 16, 64, and 256. Repeated paired trials accept protected and independent same-class controls, while correct O(n log n) and O(n^2) controls produce every benchmark output and consistently fail scaling.
